text:
eden: Compliance asked we tighten SIEM raw export retention. Idea: default 7d delete, JIT 90d via ticketed KMS unwrap. playback UI for analysts (redacted). raw exports only to siem-privileged role. thoughts?

sam: +1. main ops risk is lifecycle race where object deletes during extension. we need atomic hold tagging before unwrap.

gloria: agree. add chain-of-custody logs: actor, role, ticket, approver, cmk_grant_id. legal holds auto-approve but still logged.

kms-bot: Reminder: current CMK policy prohibits cross-account grants. proxy approach recommended: KMS-proxy issues ephemeral plaintext to stream-only handler.

eden: preferred flow: (1) ticket + approver -> (2) tag object with hold=1 -> (3) KMS-proxy issues timeboxed unwrap -> (4) viewer streams decrypted bytes (no disk) -> (5) hold removed when ticket expires.

sam: can we avoid copying to an extended bucket? copying costs money and adds complexity. proxy+hold is good. ensure lifecycle rules ignore hold tag.

compliance: also require PII redaction in playback; raw access requires justification in ticket. provide sample audit record schema: event_id, actor, actor_role, ticket_id, action, object_key, cmk_id, grant_id, timestamp, justification, approver, redaction_level.

oncall: runbook note: add emergency bypass contact and a Sev path if logs aren't reachable during triage. we had a blocked triage last month.

gloria: follow-ups: sam to prototype atomic tag + proxy sequence (ETA 1 week), eden to update policy draft, compliance to validate audit schema, oncall to update runbook. we'll reconvene Wed.

kms-bot: CMK rotation in 28 days. validate grants won't break.

eden: thanks all. I'll open GH issue and sequence diagram. meeting invite for Wed sent.
